brief: Six things that only break once real users arrive

slots.subtitle: Six failures that no test catches, because every one of them needs a real person behaving normally.

slots.title: Everyone arrives at once, or not at all
slots.subtitle: Traffic is never the smooth curve a load test produces. It is flat, then vertical, then flat again.
slots.b1Title: The pool runs out before the database does
slots.b1Body: Connections are the ceiling, and the ceiling is a default nobody chose.
slots.b2Title: Retries turn a blip into an outage
slots.b2Body: Every client retrying at once is a second, larger wave arriving on a weakened service.
slots.b3Body: Averaged over a minute, a thirty-second failure is a small dip nobody investigates.

slots.title: Nothing is load-bearing until it is missing
slots.subtitle: A cache that has never been empty in production is an assumption, not a component.
slots.b1Title: Cold start is the real capacity test
slots.b1Body: Whatever the database handles with an empty cache is your actual limit.
slots.b2Body: Which means the riskiest moment is the one you schedule deliberately.
slots.b3Body: A miss is a valid outcome, so nothing anywhere raises an alarm about it.

slots.title: Users do things nobody thought to forbid
slots.subtitle: Not maliciously. They paste a document, refresh twice, leave a tab open for four days.
slots.b1Body: A page open since Tuesday is running code and holding tokens from Tuesday.
slots.b2Body: If the button does not respond in a second, a reasonable person presses it again.
slots.b3Body: Every input limit assumed a keyboard. None of them survive forty pages of text.

slots.title: The error you never see is the expensive one
slots.subtitle: Failures that are caught, logged and swallowed look identical to nothing happening at all.
slots.b1Title: A caught exception is still a failure
slots.b1Body: Somebody did not get what they came for, and the log entry is the only trace.
slots.b2Title: Nobody reads a log with no reader
slots.b2Body: If it does not page someone or appear on a screen, it is a diary, not monitoring.
slots.b3Title: Users do not report, they leave
slots.b3Body: The ratio is roughly one report per hundred people who simply gave up.

slots.title: The data drifts while the code stands still
slots.subtitle: Nothing was deployed and the behaviour changed anyway, which is the hardest bug to believe in.
slots.b1Body: A query that was instant on a thousand rows is a timeout on a million.
slots.b2Body: Every field added later is empty on everything created before it existed.
slots.b3Title: The fix is a migration, not a patch
slots.b3Body: Which is why it gets deferred, and why it is worse the next time it surfaces.

slots.title: None of these were found by being careful
slots.subtitle: Every one of them was found by traffic, and the only variable you control is how fast you notice.
slots.b1Body: Two people reading a diff cannot simulate a thousand people at once.
slots.b2Body: No real data, no real concurrency, and nobody behaving unpredictably in it.
slots.b3Title: Optimise for the time to notice
slots.b3Body: You cannot predict the cause. You can absolutely shorten the gap before you see it.

slots.ctaBody: Empty the cache, pull a connection, paste forty pages into the input. On a Tuesday it is an experiment; at three in the morning it is an incident.
slots.closingLine: You do not get to choose the failure. You do get to choose when you meet it.
slots.signoff: The recovery is the only part you control
